title: Space and restriction

D0.outcome: Explains a space advantage as having more safe squares and posts for pieces behind advanced pawns, one that persists without needing immediate threats.

D1.outcome: In a given position, says who has more space and which enemy pieces lack safe squares.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, picks quiet restriction (deny the freeing break) over a showy threat, and watches for the liberating sacrifice or exchange.

D3.outcome: Predicts when space becomes a liability (overextended pawns become targets) and which break frees the cramped side.

misconceptions: Space must be backed by piece activity everywhere.
sources: sources/sheets/znosko-borovsky_middle-game.md §5 item 9 (space can keep growing is overstated)
conditions: The opponent's pieces really have no safe squares and no pawn break.
Unlike a time lead, a space lead does not decay; but watch for a liberating sacrifice by the strangled side.
contrasts: The same space, but a freeing pawn lever exists.
'a space advantage can keep growing without limit' is overstated; breaks and counter-sacrifices undermine it.
An opened position where space does not matter.

soft_prereq_notes.POS.BREAKS.D1: the freeing break is what a space advantage must watch
